title: An ideal-power torsion module has a presentation by cyclic ideal-power quotients
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal and $Q$ an $R$-module such that every $q\in Q$ is annihilated by $I^n$ for some $n\ge1$. There are a set $J$, positive integers $n_j$ for $j\in J$, the $R$-module $P=\bigoplus_{j\in J}R/I^{n_j}$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] of the quotient modules $R/I^{n_j}$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module], and a surjective $R$-linear map $p:P\to Q$. Its kernel $K$ is itself $I$-power torsion: every $k\in K$ is annihilated by $I^n$ for some $n\ge1$. Consequently $0\to K\to P\xrightarrow{p}Q\to0$, with $K\to P$ the inclusion, is a short exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05E8 (lemma-I-power-torsion-presentation, line 24002), first step of its proof

proof.text: Take $J=Q$ as index set. For $q\in Q$ let $n_q$ be the smallest integer $n\ge1$ with $I^nq=0$, which exists by hypothesis (for $q=0$, $n_q=1$). Define $\varphi_q:R/I^{n_q}\to Q$ by $\varphi_q(r+I^{n_q})=rq$. It is well defined: if $r-r'\in I^{n_q}$ then $(r-r')q=0$ because $I^{n_q}q=0$ means that every element of $I^{n_q}$ kills $q$. It is $R$-linear since $(r+I^{n_q})+(r'+I^{n_q})=(r+r')+I^{n_q}$ and $s(r+I^{n_q})=sr+I^{n_q}$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module], and $\varphi_q(1+I^{n_q})=q$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05E8 (lemma-I-power-torsion-presentation), proof, first two sentences

proof.text: Put $P=\bigoplus_{q\in Q}R/I^{n_q}$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] and define $p:P\to Q$ by $p((x_q)_q)=\sum_{q}\varphi_q(x_q)$; the sum is finite because $x_q=0$ for all but finitely many $q$, and $p$ is $R$-linear because addition and scalar multiplication in $P$ are componentwise and each $\varphi_q$ is $R$-linear (step 1). Then $p\circ\iota_q=\varphi_q$ for the canonical inclusion $\iota_q$, so $p(\iota_q(1+I^{n_q}))=q$ for every $q\in Q$ and $p$ is surjective. This is the canonical surjection $\bigoplus_{m\in M}R/I^{n_m}\to M\to0$ of the source.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05E8 (lemma-I-power-torsion-presentation), proof, first two sentences

proof.text: $P$ is $I$-power torsion, hence so is $K=\ker p\subseteq P$. First, $I^{n}$ kills $R/I^{n}$: for $a\in I^n$, $a(r+I^n)=ar+I^n=0+I^n$ since $ar\in I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Let $x\in P$; it is the finite sum $x=\sum_{q\in F}\iota_q(x_q)$ over the finite set $F$ of $q$ with $x_q\neq0$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Put $N=\max(\{1\}\cup\{n_q:q\in F\})$. For $q\in F$ we have $I^N\subseteq I^{n_q}$, so every $a\in I^N$ kills $x_q$, hence $a\iota_q(x_q)=\iota_q(ax_q)=0$, and $ax=0$. Thus $I^Nx=0$. In particular every $k\in K$, being an element of $P$, is annihilated by some $I^N$, $N\ge1$: the kernel is $I$-power torsion, as the source states.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05E8 (lemma-I-power-torsion-presentation), proof, first two sentences

proof.text: Exactness. In the abelian category of $R$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], monomorphisms are the injective maps, epimorphisms the surjective maps, and kernels and images are the set-theoretic ones. The inclusion $k:K\to P$ is injective, $p$ is surjective (step 2), $p\circ k=0$, and the image of $k$ is $K=\ker p$. So $0\to K\xrightarrow{k}P\xrightarrow{p}Q\to0$ is a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].
